1me4od7:2015: CI T's enterprise-level intelligent operations best practices based on Amazon Bedrock AgentCore and OpenClaw by awschina on 17 April 2026 in DevOps Permalink Share Abstract: The intelligent operations solution built by CI T together with AWS targets the cross-regional operational complexity challenges faced by global IoT businesses, using a Multi-Agent collaboration architecture design. Through a Supervisor Agent that orchestrates five specialized Agents (FinOps, Platform Ops, Security Ops, Connectivity Ops, BizOps), combined with Skills-based encapsulation and automated inspection, and based on Amazon Bedrock AgentCore's Serverless deployment, it realizes the intelligent operations transformation from “passive response” to “proactive discovery”, significantly improving operational efficiency and reducing costs. Table of Contents 01 I. Introduction: Operations challenges under globalized business 02 II. Solution: Multi-Agent collaboration architecture based on OpenClaw 03 III. Key design: “Skills-ization” of operations capabilities 04 IV. Automated inspection system: from “people finding issues” to “issues finding people” 05 V. Enterprise-grade deployment based on Amazon Bedrock AgentCore 06 VI. Summary and practical insights I. Introduction: Operations challenges under globalized business In the smart home and IoT field, building a cloud-native platform capable of supporting global business has become a core competitive advantage for enterprises. CI T provides solutions for a globally leading home environment health company whose business spans the world. To support real-time cross-regional access from massive devices, we built a global multi-region deployment architecture with AWS IoT Core at its core, deeply integrating AWS Lambda, storage, and various data analytics services to form a complete data processing pipeline. [Figure 1] However, as system scale continues to evolve and business boundaries expand, traditional operations models are facing serious challenges: Cross-regional complexity: Operations data and cost data are scattered across independent accounts in different regions, requiring frequent context switching for fault location. Expert experience is hard to scale: Deep log analysis and cost optimization rely heavily on experienced engineers; for a global-scale system, manual operations are not only inefficient but also error-prone. Inspections lag behind: Relying on manual Dashboard queries often only allows passive response after problems occur. II. Solution: Multi-Agent collaboration architecture based on OpenClaw We built an orchestratable AI Agent system that transforms complex operations capabilities into systematic automated flows. The core of this architecture lies in specialized division of labor and hierarchical scheduling: Task orchestration center: The Supervisor Agent serves as the “brain” of the entire system, responsible for splitting global tasks, scheduling sub-Agents, and aggregating final analysis results. It ensures that even for cross-domain complex operations requests, AI can provide complete, logically clear responses. Domain expert team: Specialized sub-Agents. We defined five domain Agents based on operations scenarios, each focusing on deep analysis in its specific domain: FinOps Agent (cost expert): Responsible for cost trend analysis, anomaly detection at the service/region dimension, and providing targeted optimization recommendations. Platform Ops Agent (platform expert): Digs into system logs for anomaly detection and service health assessment. Security Ops Agent (security expert): Focuses on permission control analysis, credential checks, and identification of various security risks. Connectivity Ops Agent (network expert): Monitors network latency, traffic anomalies, and SSL certificate validity to ensure global connection stability. BizOps Agent (business metrics expert): Analyzes user behavior trends and business metrics so that operations data can directly serve business decisions. III. Key design: “Skills-ization” of operations capabilities In this architecture, we used a key concept: Skills. Agents no longer hard-code calls to underlying cloud service APIs; instead, they achieve goals by invoking encapsulated, standardized skills. Why do we need a Skills layer? Encapsulate complex logic: Wrap complex AWS CLI or API calls into reusable atomic capabilities. Decouple underlying dependencies: Reduce dependence on specific tools or APIs and provide a unified interface. Capability accumulation: All operational experience is converted into system assets through Skills, rather than existing only in engineers' minds. [Figure 2] Taking the cost analysis Skill as an example, it integrates data queries from Cost Explorer in AWS MCP services and pricing estimation support from Pricing. The Agent only needs to issue the instruction “analyze AWS costs for the last three months”, and the Skill automatically completes multi-dimensional data retrieval and preliminary processing, ultimately generating a cost analysis report. [Figure 3] IV. Automated inspection system: from “people finding issues” to “issues finding people” Through OpenClaw-driven automated inspection, we transformed operations from “passive response” to “proactive discovery”.
